svg.text: The real open-source landscape (every one of these
independently verified, not taken on an AI summary's word)
Agent holds secrets but no direct network access;
Pipelock holds network access but no agent secrets.
Emits mediator-signed action receipts per call,
offline-verifiable proof of which agent/thread did
what, without a shared credential ever being
"Cloudflare for AI agents", wraps an MCP server
detection. Outbound: scans responses for 14 secret
+ 5 PII patterns before they reach the LLM. YAML
Not authorization, see the Big Tech diagram for why
languages. The decision is plain code, an LLM
cannot argue its way past a Rego or Cedar policy. A
platform can already build its own capability gate
on top of either engine directly.
issued after a local attestor verifies HOW a process
launched, distinguishes process A from process B on
the same host, even sharing one container image
The agent LOOP runs in Coder's control plane, never
inside the workspace, so a workspace never holds
an LLM-calling credential at all, by construction. No
dedicated agent firewall or per-project RBAC
described in their own docs, though.
None of these is a substitute for the others, and none of them is "infrastructure"
Every tool above is a layer you bolt onto a network/containers/agents you already have. A platform that provisions the network, the egress
firewall, and the containers itself gets that isolation by construction, the tools above add it gets deployed in the first place. The ideas above are
worth adopting selectively, see the full research for exactly which two.
